subject: ClearWave performance discovery — streaming SLOs & cost tradeoffs
messages:
From: Alicia Park <alicia@clearwave.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc:   eng@clearwave.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearWave / Redwood — follow-up on perf targets and streaming needs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so your side can size the pilot:

Summary of our goals
- Primary UX SLO: p95 latency for user-facing short responses (<= 150ms) for single-turn queries.
- Streaming requirement: for long-form answers (~400-1300 tokens) we need first-token < 350ms and steady token stream thereafter (~15-25 tok/sec).
- Concurrency: expected peak concurrent requests ~300 (web app), typical baseline 120.
- Throughput: target ~5k requests/min in peak bursts, average ~800/min.

Constraints
- Cost sensitivity: budget target is ~$X per 1M tokens (will share exact budget with sales).
- Data: request traces have repeated prefixes (same prompt families) — caching could help.

What we asked for on the call
1) A short proposal with recommended model variants and quantization profiles that meet SLOs while staying within cost guardrails.
2) A proposed benchmark plan (what you need from our side and what you'll run).
3) Timeline for a 2-week pilot with pass/fail criteria.

Attachments: I attached our SLO ask doc (clearwave-slo-ask.pdf) with examples and traces.

Can you send a proposal and a short mutual action plan by EOD Thursday?

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Park
Head of Product
ClearWave

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClearWave / Redwood — follow-up on perf targets and streaming needs

Thanks Alicia — great call. Attaching a compact proposal (redwood-slo-proposal.xlsx) and a short benchmark plan. High-level notes below so we align on expectations before the pilot.

Quick alignment (our read of your ask)
- Short responses: p95 <=150ms is achievable with the right model variant + continuous batching + a dedicated warm pool for hot prefixes.
- Streaming: first-token targets are usually dominated by single-token latency; we can get <350ms first token on GPU with streaming-optimized kernels and small batch windows.
- Concurrency/throughput: for the numbers you quoted (peak 300 concurrent, 5k RPM), we recommend a small dedicated pool (4x A100 equivalent) with autoscale headroom for bursts or a Dedicated Reservation.

Cost/performance levers we recommend to hit SLOs
1) Continuous batching (adaptive window): keeps per-token overhead low while maintaining latency SLOs for short responses. We'll tune batch windows per-path (short vs long responses).
2) Prefix/KV caching: since you have repeated prompt families, prefix caching will reduce compute for repeated calls by serving cached KV states for common prefixes.
3) Model variants + quantization: use rw-medium-quant (int8) for baseline conversational paths; reserve rw-large (fp16) for high-quality long answers or re-ranks. We expect ~40-55% cost reduction on medium quant vs fp16 with small quality delta per your eval set.
4) Streaming-optimized execution: enable attention kernel path optimized for token-at-a-time streaming to reduce first-token latency.
5) Graceful fallback routing: route to cheaper variants under sustained load with soft degradation (and a small increase in latency).

Pilot plan (2 weeks)
- Week 0 (pre-work): ClearWave provides a sample traffic trace + 50 representative prompts, and a small test API token.
- Week 1: Redwood runs bench profiles (short-response latency, streaming first-token, sustained throughput).
- Week 2: Joint smoke tests in a staging pool + tuning; produce pass/fail report.

Pass criteria
- Short-response p95 <= 150ms over 1h sustained test at baseline concurrency (120).
- Streaming first-token < 350ms and steady stream >= 12 tok/sec on 95% of tokens.
- End-to-end cost estimate within the budget band you provide.

Action items
- Jonas: share proposal + benchmark plan (attached).
- ClearWave: share trace + 50 prompts; confirm budget band.
- Ben: run initial perf profiles after we get traces.
- Neha/Marissa: prepping contract & pilot PO template.

We can run the initial bench as soon as you drop the trace. Proposed pilot kickoff: next Monday (Apr 6) if that works.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-slo-proposal.xlsx

Jonas — this is helpful, thank you. A few clarifications from Eng: 

- We'll provide the trace and the 50 prompts by EOD today (anonymized).
- For cost band: we're aiming to stay below $750 per 1M tokens as an upper bound for the pilot.
- For quality-sensitive flows we may accept a slightly slower fallback if it preserves answer quality — we want to see the quality delta numbers for medium-quant vs large-fp16.

Two asks before kickoff: 
1) Can you share an anonymized benchmark sample (single-run without full client data) so our infra team can validate measurement methodology?
2) Do you have a short checklist of required network/firewall rules for the staging pool?

Also — curious if you can include a quick breakdown of token-cost sensitivity across the levers (rough % change by switching quant/using cache/enable continuous batching). If you can fold that into the workbook, that will help procurement.

We'll plan to confirm kickoff on Monday once we finish sanitizing traces.

Best,
Alicia
